title: Relief on the Stage Fee Where Written Cancellation Notice Was Given
content:
# Relief on the Stage Fee Where Written Cancellation Notice Was Given

An owner of a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects who puts a cancellation in writing early enough is charged a smaller part of the stage fee, because notice in hand lets the company release crews and orders before the cost is committed.

## Rule

Where a confirmed written cancellation notice stands on the project record and it reached the office more than 30 days before the day installation was booked to begin, the stage fee is taken at half the rate the stage carries, that is at 50 per cent of it.

Where a confirmed written cancellation notice stands on the project record and it reached the office 30 days or fewer before that booked day, or after it, the stage fee is taken at three quarters of the rate the stage carries, that is at 75 per cent of it.

Where no confirmed written cancellation notice stands on the project record, the stage fee is taken at the rate the stage carries in full.

## Both sides of the boundary

The lead is counted from the day the notice was recorded to the day installation was booked to begin. A lead of 31 days or more is more than 30 days and takes the first case; a lead of exactly 30 days is not more than 30 and takes the second, as does any shorter lead and any notice recorded after the booked day.

| Confirmed written notice on the record | Days from the notice to the booked installation day | Portion of the stage fee taken |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 45 | 50 per cent |
| yes | 31 | 50 per cent |
| yes | 30 | 75 per cent |
| yes | 4 | 75 per cent |
| yes | the notice came after the booked day | 75 per cent |
| no | — | the whole of it |

## Worked figures (hypothetical stage fee of USD 12000 before relief)

Notice recorded 40 days before the booked start: USD 6000.00 is charged. Notice recorded 12 days before it: USD 9000.00. No confirmed written notice on the record: USD 12000.00.
